application.cv_markdown:
Heikki Virtanen

Location: Oulu

EDUCATION

Salsette Institute of Technology Bombay (SIT Bombay)
B.Tech + M.Tech (Dual Degree), Metallurgical Engineering and Materials Science — 2008

CAREER HISTORY

Boreal Photonics — Signal Processing Engineer
2009 – present

I joined Boreal Photonics in 2009, shortly after returning to Finland from my studies in India. My work at Boreal has been centred on materials characterisation and optical thin-film analysis for the company’s photonic component product line. This includes spectrophotometry, ellipsometry, and surface-roughness measurement of deposited thin films, as well as process-parameter optimisation for the coating deposition systems.

Day-to-day responsibilities:
- Thin-film thickness and uniformity measurement using spectrophotometric and ellipsometric techniques
- Process documentation and batch-record analysis for optical coating deposition runs
- Coordination with the optical design team on coating specification compliance
- Internal training of junior technicians on measurement procedures and equipment operation

All technical communication at Boreal Photonics is in English, including internal reports, process documentation, and correspondence with international suppliers and coating-material vendors. I have worked in English throughout my tenure.

Relocated from Helsinki to Oulu in 2009 to join Boreal Photonics; have been based at the Oulu facility for the full duration of my employment.

PROJECTS AND PUBLICATIONS

Thin-Film Characterisation Methods
Co-authored a paper on spectrophotometric methods for multilayer thin-film thickness determination, published in Thin Film Metrology Letters (Aldenbrook Scientific, 2015). The paper reported a measurement protocol developed internally at Boreal and validated against reference samples from PTB (Germany’s national metrology institute).

Open-Source Contribution
Contributed MATLAB image-analysis and profile-extraction routines to “CoatingAnalysis,” an open-source thin-film characterisation toolkit hosted on GitHub (~80 stars). The contribution included automated fringe-counting algorithms for interference-based thickness measurement.

EU Kestrel 2020: OPTISENSE (2018–2020)
Participated in the OPTISENSE project, responsible for Boreal’s coating characterisation deliverables. Finnish citizen; full EU work authorisation. No restrictions on employment or project-clearance eligibility.

SKILLS AND LANGUAGES

Spectrophotometry, ellipsometry, profilometry, SEM/EDX
MATLAB, LabVIEW, ImageJ
Finnish (native), English (professional working), Hindi (conversational)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Kaikuvaara Oy,

Please consider this letter as my application for the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position. I appreciate that my CV is not the typical profile for this role, and I want to be upfront about that — but I would also like to explain why I think the move makes sense, and what I would bring with me.

My career has followed an unusual path. I grew up in Helsinki, went to SIT Bombay for a dual degree in Metallurgical Engineering and Materials Science, and returned to Finland in 2009 to join Boreal Photonics in Oulu. At Boreal, I have spent seventeen years doing materials characterisation and thin-film analysis for the company’s photonic component line — spectrophotometry, ellipsometry, surface-roughness measurement, and process optimisation for coating deposition systems. The work is precise and measurement-intensive, and it has given me a strong foundation in experimental rigour, calibration discipline, and systematic data analysis.

What it has not given me is the kind of signal-processing depth that Kaikuvaara’s role calls for, and I want to be straightforward about that. My formal training is in metallurgy, not electrical engineering, and my daily work at Boreal is closer to materials science than to algorithm design or embedded firmware development. But I have spent nearly two decades inside a photonics company, sitting next to optical and electronic engineers, reviewing their specifications, and understanding how measurement, characterisation, and process control fit into an instrument-development workflow. That cross-disciplinary exposure is not something you get from a textbook, and I believe it would transfer into the kind of systems-level environment that Kaikuvaara operates in.

The reason I am looking to move now is that I have taken my current role at Boreal as far as it can go. I have published in the field, contributed to open-source tooling, worked on EU-funded projects, and trained the next generation of technicians on our measurement procedures. The work is good, but I have been doing essentially the same thing for seventeen years, and I want a technical environment that pushes me further. Kaikuvaara’s instrument work — SAR payloads, scatterometer electronics, readout chains — represents the kind of system-level engineering challenge that I find compelling, and I would rather make a lateral move into a harder domain than continue in a comfortable one.

I have lived in Oulu since 2009 and have no intention of leaving. I know the engineering community here well, I have watched the remote-sensing and wireless cluster grow from a handful of companies to the concentration it is today, and I am genuinely interested in what Kaikuvaara is building. If there is a path into the team — even if it starts in a measurement, characterisation, or test-support capacity rather than a signal-processing design role — I would welcome the chance to explore it.

I am available for a conversation at your convenience and happy to answer any questions about my background.

Best regards,
Heikki Virtanen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
